title: Zayd chooses
hook: Zayd, a freed boy in the house, chooses to stay with him rather than go home with his own father

segments.voice: Yesterday: their children. Four daughters, and little sons who died, whose names the sources keep. Your line was: every child remembered.

A father has been looking for his son for a long time. The boy was taken in a raid, the sirah says, and sold in a market far from home. The father mourned him in verse: I weep for Zayd, and I don't know what became of him. Then word comes. The boy is alive, in Mecca, in the house of a man of Quraysh, Muhammad ibn Abdullah. The father and his brother ride south with money to buy him back. They find him. And the boy says no.
screen: `A BOY TAKEN IN A RAID.` → `A FATHER WEEPS IN VERSE.` → `THE BOY SAYS NO.`

segments.voice: Here's how the sirah tells it. Zayd ibn Harithah came into the house as a gift. Khadijah's nephew had bought him, she received him, and she gave him to her husband, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. When Zayd's father, Harithah, arrived with the ransom, the Prophet didn't haggle. He said, in the account Ibn Sa'd keeps: call him, and let him choose. If he chooses you, he's yours, with no price. If he chooses me, I'm not a man to turn away someone who chooses me. So they called Zayd. Do you know these men? Yes, my father and my uncle. And Zayd said: I won't choose anyone over you. His father was stunned. You'd choose slavery over your own father and family? Zayd answered that he had seen something in this man he would never trade. Then the Prophet took him by the hand to the gathering place by the Ka'ba and said: bear witness, Zayd is my son. The father, the report says, went home at peace. People called him Zayd ibn Muhammad until a verse came, Sahih al-Bukhari records, and Pickthall renders its opening: "Proclaim their real parentage." So he was Zayd ibn Harithah again, his own father's son. But the bond stayed, and the Qur'an, at surah thirty-three, verse thirty-seven, mentions Zayd by name. A boy who chose a house, kept in the Book.
screen: `A GIFT IN KHADIJAH'S HOUSE.` · `CALL HIM, AND LET HIM CHOOSE.` · `BEAR WITNESS, ZAYD IS MY SON.` · `HIS OWN FATHER'S NAME RESTORED.` · then, large: `HE CHOSE TO STAY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who chose you when they didn't have to: a friend who stayed, a stepparent, a teacher who took a chance. Hold their face a moment and ask what it cost them. If you pray, thank Allah for them by name; if not, let the gratitude sit in your chest a while.
Zayd chooses. Offered his freedom and his father's home, Zayd ibn Harithah chose to stay with the Prophet, who then called him his son. Today's word.
Your line: he chose to stay. Chosen freely, and kept in the Book. That's day seven hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Zayd ibn Harithah as a beloved companion of the Prophet ﷺ, and his story is told when teaching about the Qur'an's ruling that adopted children keep their birth parents' names.

notes: The father's search, his verse of mourning, the choice and the declaration at the Ka'ba follow Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Hisham's notes; the dialogue is paraphrased. Confirm the sequence (freedom and adoption after the choice) and that 'the father went home at peace' is in the report.
Hook says 'taken in a raid' and 'sold in a market far from home' (the market at Ukaz in some reports); confirm.
Index hook calls Zayd 'a freed boy'; in the reports he is freed and adopted after his choice. Script follows the reports; suggest the index read 'a boy in the house'.
Pickthall 33:5 opening quoted from memory; confirm wording.
The later marriage of Zayd and Zaynab bint Jahsh (33:37) is not told here; only that the verse names him.
Editor: hook no longer says the father learned of 'a man called al-Amin' (the reports of the search don't use the title); it now names the house as that of Muhammad ibn Abdullah of Quraysh.
Audit: read in full; Ibn Sa'd sequence, Bukhari 4782 and the 33:5 / 33:37 references are consistent with the reports. No changes.
